proof_audit.continuous_time: Hazards are finite inverse-time quantities; matched transitions use first-dt equations and exact two-state endpoint probabilities, not raw annual intensities. Aggregate continuum transition law is stated as a maintained assumption.
proof_audit.values_and_bargaining: Bounded discounted finite-state value verification supplied. Pair-specific wage derivatives preserve outside values. Nash log objective is strictly concave with unattainable low-surplus endpoints, establishing positive-share solution; total surplus incorporates future worker opportunities.
proof_audit.equilibrium: All primitive domains stated. Continuous strictly increasing H constructs and characterizes the unique active stationary equilibrium. Inactive boundary uses agreement and recruiting-cost inequalities rather than q at zero. Other endpoint primitive regimes are explicitly excluded. Positive-surplus inactivity is excluded under the explicitly stated limiting-entry convention by a positive prospective entrant value. Planner positive-root analysis expressly maintains y>b.
proof_audit.shocks: Only an unanticipated permanent productivity shift with immediate renegotiation and vacancy adjustment is solved. Individual values can jump because aggregate current unemployment does not change per-agent hazards at fixed tightness; stock unemployment remains continuous. General future-shock equations have the omitted derivative or conditional expectation terms identified.
proof_audit.planner: Locally bounded measurable controls give unique absolutely continuous u in[0,1]. Real output/home utility are bounded, discounted costs finite or dominated at minus infinity. Affine candidate, global g maximum and positive scalar root imply a Bellman inequality for all states/controls. The finite-T chain-rule bound and bounded terminal remainder prove global discounted optimality against time-varying controls. Strict g and positive u at t>0 give uniqueness almost everywhere. Same initial u and all owners/workers are included.
proof_audit.hosios: η=α equates the market and planner roots; unique inversion for η at a positive θ proves necessity. Comparative static in η gives the over/under-entry directions. No universal extension to non-CRS, insurance taxation, heterogeneity or constrained finance is asserted.
proof_audit.financing: Owners explicitly finance recruiting from wealth or enforceable frictionless claims; no free grant. Baseline and shock cases additionally exhibit owned interest-earning reserves sufficient for every recruiting date. Recruiting is deducted once and wages cancel. Zero vacancy NPV never removes κ.
proof_audit.identification: An original observational-equivalence pair leaves all baseline market moments equal while changing matching elasticity and efficiency. Steady inversion is shown false on an exact transition point. Estimation/measurement restrictions are separated from assumed calibration.

exercise_audit.v14-c04-e1: First-dt flow difference, full integrating-factor solution, two endpoint transition probabilities allowing repeated switching, exact case values and distinction from first-finding survival. All time units and initial conditions supplied.
exercise_audit.v14-c04-e2: All four value equations derived from the same short-interval timing; bounded terminal remainder gives values. Ownership and financing explicitly stipulated. Pair wage variation holds U,V fixed; strict log Nash objective gives unique surplus shares and the wage formula, with positive recruiting cost despite V=0.
exercise_audit.v14-c04-e3: Continuous H, strict increase, negative origin and divergent upper tail establish a unique root for y>b; every original equation reconstructed with positive surpluses. For y<=b agreement inequalities establish inactivity without evaluating q0. Baseline private values, stocks, flows and consolidated real accounts all derived.
exercise_audit.v14-c04-e4: Implicit differentiation covers all seven requested primitive effects. Baseline four requested derivatives are exact; all signs use the declared interior domain. The causal-inference caveat identifies omitted co-moving primitives rather than treating a theoretical derivative as data.
exercise_audit.v14-c04-e5: Permanent surprise changes values and vacancies but preserves unemployment continuity; all new rates and values, exact half-gap state/drift and false stationary inversion derived. Exact discounted costs and sufficient reserve distinguish funding from income. Anticipated/temporary/recurrent changes require forward value terms.
exercise_audit.v14-c04-e6: Planner objective uses real b and worker-plus-owner surplus with a common initial state and the same financing authority. Strict global stage concavity, scalar root, coefficient matching and finite-T integrated inequality prove attainment against all locally bounded admissible time-varying controls. Bounded affine W removes terminal remainder. Positive unemployment for t>0 makes strict maximizing control unique almost everywhere. Inversion proves both directions of Hosios within the model.
exercise_audit.v14-c04-e7: Distorted η=1/3 equilibrium and own-policy affine evaluation are derived independently. The two values are compared from identical u0=1/11, so the 3/55 loss is not a misleading comparison of different initial steady states. Real vacancy costs explain higher welfare despite higher long-run unemployment; distributional compensation is not assumed.
exercise_audit.v14-c04-e8: General α=1/2 quadratic selects unique positive root for y>b. Actual entry residual at θhat=121/100 is1/16, certified θ error1/4 and actual21/100. Bisection sign/interval proof and residual derivative lower bound are stated, and inactive regimes are explicitly routed outside positive-root iteration.
exercise_audit.v14-c04-e9: α=1/2 and1/3 with A=1 fit the same θ=f=q=1 and all baseline market values, while only one satisfies Hosios. Bargaining identification is conditional on independently known other primitives. Exact stationary Beveridge curve and its negative log slope derived; nonstationary state equation and credible identifying variation addressed.
exercise_audit.v14-c04-e10: Five concrete errors repaired: rates versus probabilities, zero NPV versus recruiting finance, fit versus identification, unemployment versus same-state discounted welfare, and benefits transfers versus real output. Five two-point criteria give an explicit ten-point critique rubric with no policy-position credit.
